markdown_report:
**Prioritize padding-safe GRU encoding before another cropping experiment.** At 0% progress, this offers a small, testable intervention grounded in the supplied measurements.

**Starting-point insights.** (1) All four categories fail the declared padding tolerance; the latest maximum errors range from 0.00101 to 0.00234. This warrants localization before interpreting context interventions. (2) Matched prefix removal reduces margins in every category. These checkpoint interventions provide no evidence that cropped training improves validation. (3) Movies_and_TV has the latest highest sampled misranking rate, 4.92%. Training-pair separation nevertheless cannot establish host HR@10 or willingness to choose now.

**Related-work insights.** (1) PyTorch’s [GRU equations](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html) permit hidden-state changes under zero input. Explicitly skipping padded steps therefore addresses a plausible mechanism. (2) PyTorch’s [numerical-accuracy guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/numerical_accuracy.html) explains why batch-shape changes can introduce numerical differences. Padding discrepancies require controlled localization rather than automatic attribution to a recurrence bug. (3) [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show limitations of sampled ranking metrics. Supplementary audits should inform interpretation while the pinned host metric controls selection.

**Framework and directions.** Organize development into encoding correctness, ranking evidence, and context utility:

| Direction | Existing evidence | Proposed next step |
|---|---|---|
| Encoding correctness | Padding discrepancies | Canonical valid-token recurrence and predictor parity |
| Ranking evidence | Sampled pair margins | Withheld training-prefix rank audits |
| Context utility | Harmful prefix deletion | Matched-supervision cropping after correctness checks |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Canonical padding-safe GRU | 3/8/4 | Direct, reusable correctness intervention | Established packing technique; accuracy benefit unknown |
| Fixed training-prefix boundary audit | 4/7/4 | Measures ranking near the top-10 cutoff | Supplementary evidence may disagree with host validation |
| Matched-target suffix augmentation | 4/6/5 | Separates context removal from supervision allocation | Removes useful history and adds experimental cost |

**Selected algorithm.** Retain the supplied GRU4Rec and canonicalize real tokens before recurrence: gather chronological nonpadding embeddings, right-pad internally, pack nonempty rows, run the existing GRU, unpack, and scatter features to original positions. Read the greatest valid original index. Preserve existing transformations, dropout placement, loss, optimizer and sampler; retain an already-correct implementation.

Compare equivalent histories under extra leading padding, individual and permuted-batch execution, and checkpoint/predictor reconstruction. Record feature errors, score errors and top-10 changes against repeat-run numerical variation. Retrain one independent model per category only if encoding changes; preserve all four routes, seeds, 200 batches/epoch, maximum 200 epochs and the shared budget. Select using unchanged macro validation HR@10. No validation improvement is currently established.

idea.description: Localize the reported padding discrepancies and, where necessary, implement canonical valid-token encoding in the supplied GRU4Rec. Preserve one independently trained model per category, aligned position-level features, final-nonpadding readout, and identical checkpoint and generated-predictor behavior.
idea.motivation: The latest supplied diagnostics report padding feature discrepancies above 1e-5 in all four categories, while matched prefix deletion reduces sampled margins. Encoding consistency is therefore a more defensible initial priority than stronger recency bias. Batch-shape numerical variation, probe mistakes, and actual padded recurrent updates remain competing explanations; the measurements do not identify the cause or establish validation gains.
idea.implementation_notes:
Start from the host's corrected baseline and preserve any implementation already handling padding correctly. Inspect behavior through the supplied interfaces during implementation rather than reconstructing unspecified architecture details. Keep all embedding transforms, recurrent layers, dropout placement, output transforms, score activation, objective, sampler and optimizer unchanged unless a specific inconsistency requires correction. Zero embedding alone does not skip GRU updates. Never pack a left-padded tensor directly using nonzero counts: compact real inputs chronologically, pack only nonempty rows, then restore B x L x H alignment. Reset recurrent state for each independent example; preserve gradients through gathered and scattered valid features. Empty rows follow the supplied baseline policy without entering packing.

Use eval mode and no gradients for diagnostic comparisons, then restore the original model mode. First compare repeated identical execution to establish numerical variation, then extra-left-padding, single-example versus batched execution, batch permutation and unrelated preceding inference calls. Report nonfinite counts, maximum absolute and relative feature/score errors, measurement counts and top-10 changes; do not silently widen the declared 1e-5 threshold. Identical predictor parity checks must include item mappings and architecture configuration. If a correction changes encoding, retrain from seed 42 rather than claiming an existing checkpoint was trained under corrected semantics.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Return metrics and metric_definitions with unavailable measurements represented explicitly. Preserve view.model as the actual nn.Module and retain item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data compatibility. Consume batches (None, sequence, positive, negative) with B x L tensors. Mask sampled-margin positions using nonzero input, positive and negative IDs. Report margins as conditional training diagnostics, not ranking accuracy or simulator traits.

Keep Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing; preprocessing seed 0; training seed 42; maximum 200 epochs; exactly 200 batches per completed epoch; DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; and trial-local artifacts. Update the embedded predictor writer with every encoding change. Each category loads exactly one independently trained checkpoint, with no averaging or auxiliary fitted scores. Preserve the host evaluator and select using its macro validation HR@10. Predeclare an affordable common training schedule using host timing and remaining shared 43,200 GPU-seconds; charge diagnostics and failed attempts. Do not read other trials, hidden tests, unavailable metadata or pretrained assets. Produce the required unseen-item full-catalog recommendations for five real training users per category without interpreting histories as ownership or compatibility labels.
idea.pseudocode:
def log2feats(sequence):
    # Integrate into the supplied model; preserve its existing transforms.
    valid = sequence.ne(0)
    lengths = valid.sum(dim=1)
    active = lengths.gt(0).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
    output = zeros(B, L, existing_feature_dimension)
    if active.numel() == 0:
        return baseline_empty_features(output)

    # Gather chronological real inputs; right padding is internal only.
    compact_ids = right_pad([sequence[b][valid[b]] for b in active])
    embedded = existing_input_pipeline(compact_ids)
    packed = pack_padded_sequence(
        embedded, lengths[active].cpu(),
        batch_first=True, enforce_sorted=False)
    packed_features, _ = existing_gru(packed, fresh_zero_state(active))
    compact_features, _ = pad_packed_sequence(
        packed_features, batch_first=True)
    compact_features = existing_output_pipeline(compact_features)
    for row, original_row in enumerate(active):
        output[original_row, valid[original_row]] = compact_features[row, :lengths[original_row]]
    return output


def final_features(sequence):
    features = log2feats(sequence)
    positions = arange(sequence.shape[1]).expand_as(sequence)
    final_index = positions.masked_fill(sequence.eq(0), -1).amax(dim=1)
    result = features[arange(sequence.shape[0]), final_index.clamp_min(0)]
    return apply_baseline_empty_history_policy(result, final_index.lt(0))

# Before changing encoding, localize discrepancies using fixed histories/candidates.
# Compare repeated runs, extra leading padding, batch composition and state reset.
# Compare live model, reconstructed checkpoint and generated predictor.
# If encoding changes, train one fresh GRU4Rec per category under the fixed schedule.
# Preserve diagnostic interfaces and update the predictor writer together.
# Obtain unchanged host macro validation HR@10; never combine model scores.

originality.positive: Combines canonical recurrent encoding with measured diagnostic and generated-predictor consistency checks tailored to this constrained GRU4Rec workflow.
originality.negative: Valid-token packing and padding-invariance checks are established engineering methods rather than a new recommendation architecture.

future_potential.positive: Consistent encoding provides a reusable foundation for interpretable context interventions and reliable deployment across history lengths.
future_potential.negative: The discrepancy may partly reflect numerical or probe behavior, and correcting it may produce little improvement in host validation HR@10.

code_difficulty.positive: The intervention can retain the GRU backbone, objective, sampling and category routing with a localized encoding change.
code_difficulty.negative: Preserving dropout semantics, aligned gradients, empty-history behavior and embedded predictor parity requires careful integration with the actual baseline.

related_work.title: PyTorch GRU documentation
contributions: Defines recurrent equations showing why zero inputs can still change hidden states.
limitations: Does not identify the cause of the supplied model's discrepancies or establish recommendation improvements.

related_work.title: PyTorch pack_padded_sequence documentation
contributions: Provides the packing primitive for processing variable-length valid sequences without padded recurrent steps.
limitations: Left-padded histories require chronological compaction before packing and output remapping afterward.

related_work.title: PyTorch Numerical accuracy
contributions: Explains that batched and sliced computations can differ numerically.
Supports separating numerical variation from semantic encoding inconsistencies.
limitations: Provides no universal acceptable error threshold for this recommender.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Analyzes limitations of sampled recommendation metrics and their relationship to full-ranking comparisons.
limitations: Does not replace the task's mandated sampled host evaluator or validate sampled training margins as a selection criterion.
